scoring_summary: server/attorneyQuality.ts exports reviewAttorneyQuality(input: {firmName, state, city, website, phone, practiceAreas, sourceUrl, discoveredVia}), a two-stage scorer. If input.sourceUrl is absent, it skips straight to deterministicFallback(): a simple rule-based score (30 pts if sourceUrl present + 25 pts if website-or-phone present + 15 pts if state present, so max 70 here since sourceUrl is absent in this branch), tier 'review' only if source+contact+state are all true else 'defer', confidence 55 if sourceUrl else 20. If sourceUrl IS present, it calls an LLM (agent 'money_maker', model 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro') whose system prompt instructs a 'cautious B2B partnership qualification reviewer' not to claim a firm handles solar matters, accepts referrals, has a decision-maker, or has capacity unless the supplied evidence proves it. The LLM returns a strict-JSON 100-point breakdown -- evidenceIntegrity (0-30), leadMarketFit (0-20), reachability (0-20), capacityProxy (0-15), partnershipReadiness (0-15) -- plus a tier, confidence, explanation, an array of pass/needs_review/blocked gates, a suggestedPitch, and nextActions. The code then overrides the LLM's own tier with a deterministic gate: tier becomes 'priority' ONLY if practiceAreas text matches /solar/i AND score>=65 AND (phone or website present); otherwise 'review' if score>=50 and sourceUrl exists; otherwise 'defer'. An extra 'Priority ranking gate' entry is appended to the gates array recording which condition applied. If the LLM call throws, the code falls back to deterministicFallback() and logs a console warning. A separate exported helper, buildLinkedInLookupUrl(firmName, state), only builds a manual LinkedIn people-search URL string -- it does not scrape or verify LinkedIn data itself.
discovery_producer_summary: server/scheduled/attorneyDiscovery.ts exports attorneyDiscoveryHandler, an Express POST handler -- it is an ingestion callback, not a scraper. It contains no code that itself fetches Justia, Google Maps, or any other external site; its own top-of-file comment says 'An isolated scheduled research agent submits only public, source-backed firm records here. The callback neither contacts a prospect nor reads LinkedIn.' It is cron-only: it 403s unless the authenticated request carries user.isCron and user.taskUid. It validates the POST body with zod: up to 8 candidates (results array), each requiring firmName (2-300 chars), state (2-50 chars), a valid sourceUrl (<=1000 chars), and an 8-500 char sourceNote, with optional city, website (valid URL), phone, and up to 8 practiceAreas strings; plus a top-level researchSummary (8-1500 chars). For each candidate it queries the attorneyProspects table for an existing row matching the same (firmName, state) pair -- a match is counted as a duplicate and skipped, otherwise a new row is inserted via buildAttorneyDiscoveryRecord(). That builder computes its own separate, simple deterministic overallScore (30 base + 15 if website present + 10 if phone present + a flat, unconditional 15 labeled 'geographicMatch' + 15 if practiceAreas is non-empty, capped at 100) -- this is a different, simpler score than the LLM-based one in attorneyQuality.ts and is not itself an LLM call. It sets outreachStatus='researching', discoveredBy='money_maker', discoveredVia='scheduled_public_research' (a literal hardcoded string in this file), sourceUrl=candidate.sourceUrl, a linkedInSearchUrl built via buildLinkedInLookupUrl(), linkedInResearchStatus='research_ready', and verifiedAt=now. After processing, it writes one summary message into agentChatThreads (agentSlug 'money_maker', 30-day expiry) reporting saved vs duplicate counts plus the echoed researchSummary, and returns {ok, saved, duplicates, candidateCount, taskUid}. Discrepancy worth flagging: docs/attorney-acquisition-status.md describes the actual upstream producer as a Justia consumer-law directory fetch (https://www.justia.com/lawyers/consumer-law/{state}/, discoveredVia: justia_public_directory, max 8 cards, dedupe on firmName+state). The max-8 cap and the (firmName, state) dedupe key in this file do match that description, but the discoveredVia string this code actually writes is the literal 'scheduled_public_research', not 'justia_public_directory' -- and the Justia-fetching logic itself is not present anywhere in this file. It must live in the calling research-agent process (a candidate is server/justiaAttorneyResearch.ts, present in this repo but outside the set of files this review was scoped to read).
